problem:
Find the **exact** solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$

**In ascending order**, the solutions are $x=$
{{field-1}}

{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
Recall that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the $4$th quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13977622/assets/17803dc8d1d3ca2e31586969797b401d5d0a2d958bd6628387b512974076df7a.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =2\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{11\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the solutions are $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ and $x=\frac{11\pi }{6}.$
